summary: Hunt for speedup/efficiency wins missed by the paper2 engine plan (CPU, algorithmic, GPU)
logs: Three hunters: CPU batched path, algorithmic/pipeline, GPU kernel design

vetted.name: Bernstein-gated deep-dip fallback (kill per-row eigvals on well-conditioned rows)
vetted.mechanism: scan_polish_from_coefs unconditionally routes every row with min|MM|<0.15*max|MM| through _exact_root_fallback = per-frequency numpy.polynomial arithmetic + companion eigvals (46x46 at H=8, ~0.8 ms/row). Replace with the per-row Bernstein density test already used by the shared_phase C3.5 machinery: a sub-grid spike requires r_min <= ((2H)*dtheta)^2/2, so compute M_needed = 2*pi*2H/sqrt(2*r_min) per flagged row; if M_needed <= current M (256 at H=8) the scan is already guaranteed-bracketing and the fallback is skipped; else rescan ONLY those rows at densified M via one extra batched circle-FFT call (n_angles arg already exists).
vetted.stage: scan maximizer, deep-dip fallback (58 ms of 269 ms at H=8; 71/4000 rows flagged on clean griz, 21% of wall for 1.8% of rows)
vetted.factor_stage: ~25x on the fallback stage on griz (58 ms -> ~2 ms; measured: ALL 71 flagged rows have r_min>=0.089 -> Bernstein M=256 = grid already used, and scan-only matches the eigvals rows to max |dP|=1.9e-16)
vetted.factor_end_to_end: 1.27x (H=8 direct-path pilot engine, 269->211 ms); ~1.1x at H=4
vetted.effort: 0.5-1 day including re-running the C3/C3.5 deep-dip fixture regression
vetted.evidence: probe2/probe5 (_hunt/): fallback = 58-70 ms; disabling it changes zero of 4000 powers by >1e-12 (max rel 1.3e-15); worst flagged r_min=0.0889 vs Bernstein spike-existence threshold 0.077 at M=256. Same one-sided-bracketing argument C3.5 adjudicated for shared_phase.
vetted.adjusted_factor: ~1.15-1.25x on the H=8 direct-path engine (fallback cost 52 ms confirmed at 0.73 ms/row; total engine 292-345 ms depending on machine load, so 1.27x is the idle-machine upper edge); ~1.05-1.1x survey end-to-end under the banked staged-H mix, because the H=4 detection arm that dominates survey cost flags only 3/4000 rows (~1.01-1.05x there, not the claimed 1.1x). Upside not in the headline: flag rate is data-dependent, so on badly-conditioned real sparse chunks (flag rate >>1.8%) the win grows toward ~2x exactly where chunks are slowest.
vetted.reasoning: Mechanism verified in the actual code: core.py:611-612/765-766 unconditionally route every min|MM|<0.15*max|MM| row through per-row companion eigvals, and the proposed gate is literally the codebase's own adjudicated machinery — core.py:385 states the ((2H)dtheta)^2/2 spike-existence bound (0.0771 at M=256/H=8, arithmetic checks) and multiband.py:646-647 already implements M_needed=2*pi*2H/sqrt(2*r_min) with the 2^20 cap for the C3.5 shared_phase path; absM min/max are already computed so the gate is free. Probe evidence reproduced exactly on rerun: 71/4000 flagged, worst r_min=0.0889>0.0771 (all 71 pass the gate; 3/3 at H=4), scan-only matches eigvals rows to max|dP|=1.9e-16, and an isolated timing of _exact_root_fallback on the 71 rows gives 52 ms (0.73 ms/row), confirming the claimed 58 ms/0.8 ms-per-row stage cost. Amdahl arithmetic is internally correct (269-56=213 -> 1.27x) but that is the idle-machine H=8 pilot number; my loaded-machine warm min-of-5 gives rest-of-engine 292 ms -> 1.16-1.18x, and the survey end-to-end under the already-banked staged-H pipeline is dominated by the nearly-unaffected H=4 arm, so ~1.05-1.1x — within the ~2x SOLID band but the 1.27x should not be quoted as survey-level. SAFE classification is honest (not FREE: sub-gate rows switch from eigvals to densified scan, the exact substitution C3.5 adjudicated as one-sided >= eigvals at deep dips where eigvals itself can fail per MB-DIP-1). Two implementation requirements: recompute the gate at the densified M instead of recursively calling scan_polish_from_coefs (naive recursion re-flags the same rows and re-enters eigvals — probe5's own densified-rescan call did exactly this), and keep eigvals where M_needed exceeds the 2^20 cap. Not double-counted against the banked C4 scan-default (this kills its residual eigvals) or the GPU Aberth rooter (Track A GPU; Paper 2 engine is CPU-only). Vet script left at experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_hunt/vet_bernstein_gate.py.

vetted.name: Newton polish 8 -> 3 steps (or early-exit on max|step|)
vetted.mechanism: _SCAN_NEWTON_STEPS=8 but the clamped Newton on dP/dtheta is quadratically convergent from grid seeds: by step 3 the powers are converged to float64. Drop to 3 steps (also shrinks the dip-refinement loop, which reuses n_newton). Optionally an early-exit when max|step| < 1e-12 for robustness on adversarial data.
vetted.stage: Newton polish + dip refine (Horner evals = 90 ms of 269 ms at H=8)
vetted.factor_stage: 1.6x on scan (190->120 ms incl. fallback at H=8; 41.5->23.1 ms at H=4); polish-only portion ~2.1x
vetted.effort: minutes for the constant; 1-2 h for a vectorized early-exit + regression
vetted.evidence: probe3: n_newton=3 vs 8 max rel dP = 2.4e-15 (H=8) and 7.4e-15 (H=4) over 4000 freqs, 0 rows differing >1e-12; n=4 is bit-cleaner still (max rel 1.9e-15) if extra margin wanted
vetted.adjusted_factor: ~1.3x end-to-end on the CPU batched multiband solve (measured 1.34x at H=4, 1.37x at H=8 with direct sums; scan-stage 1.55-1.7x). Survey-wide ~1.3x, since staged-H makes H<=4 detection the dominant term; H=8 refine work gets ~1.35-1.4x.
vetted.reasoning: Mechanism verified in-code: _SCAN_NEWTON_STEPS=8 (core.py:375) drives both the polish loop (core.py:687) and dip-refine loop (core.py:635), and the paper2 batched path multiband_power_spectrum_batched (multiband.py:1054) uses the default, fallback included. Probe3 reproduced exactly: n=3 max rel dP = 7.4e-15 (H=4) / 2.4e-15 (H=8) over 4000 freqs, 0 rows >1e-12, while n=2 breaks (4e-9) — so 3 is the genuine quadratic-convergence knee, not a myth. Timing probes (rerun single-threaded; competing job on machine, so ratios trusted over absolutes): scan stage 58.7->34.5 ms at H=4 (1.70x), 290->~160-187 ms at H=8 (~1.55-1.8x); Amdahl on measured stage shares gives batched-solve end-to-end 111.3->~83 ms (1.34x, H=4) and 391.7->~286 ms (1.37x, H=8), matching the claimed 1.31x/1.35x. No double-counting with banked wins (measured on the 12-14x batched path; GPU fused polish is a different lens). SAFE is honest: all safety nets (exact-root fallback below 0.15 rtol, seed-fallback, +/-2pi/M clamp) are step-count-independent, and the dip-refine hedge in the (0.15,0.5) band is documented non-load-bearing (core.py:388-392). Caveats for implementation: the WP C2 spec floor is 6 steps (core.py:374), so a hard n=3 needs a VERIFICATION.md amendment + rerun of the scan-polish suite and C3.5 fixtures — the early-exit variant (max|step|<1e-12, worst case still 8) preserves the spec and is cleaner; multiband.py:695/754 (C3.5-verified shared_phase) read the constant directly, so scope the change to the floating_offsets call site or use early-exit; n=4 costs only ~19% of the saving and adds margin. Evidence base is one well-conditioned synthetic source; the claimed 1-2h effort correctly includes the regression gate.

vetted.name: Provable candidate filter before polish (Bernstein gain bound)
vetted.mechanism: The scan polishes EVERY circular local max (7.3/row at H=8, 4.4/row at H=4) but polish can raise a candidate by at most gain=(pi/M)^2*(2H)^2/2 = 1.9% of P (Bernstein curvature bound at M=32H, the same bound already in the _SCAN constants comments). Drop grid-max candidates with P0 < (1-2*gain)*rowmax before the Newton loop -- they provably cannot win. Keep all dip candidates (their polish gain is not Bernstein-bounded inside deep dips).
vetted.stage: Newton polish candidate set (41.6k candidates at H=8: 29.1k maxima + 12.5k dips)
vetted.factor_stage: maxima 7.3->1.1 per row (measured); total polish candidates 41.6k->~17k = 2.4x less polish work; combined with 3-step Newton the polish stage shrinks ~4-6x (90 -> ~15-20 ms)
vetted.factor_end_to_end: ~1.13x incremental on top of the 3-step win (269 -> ~175 ms combined with wins 1-2)
vetted.effort: 2-4 h + an equivalence test vs unfiltered scan
vetted.evidence: probe3: viable-after-filter 1.08/row (H=8), 1.05/row (H=4); on rows with no dips (filter fully provable) 1.00/row. Note 98.3% of H=8 rows carry dip candidates (mean 3.1/row) which are retained
vetted.adjusted_factor: Polish Newton loop 2.3-2.6x (measured 108.9 -> 42.4 ms at H=8, 41.6k -> 18.2k candidates with the required K.18-aware variant); end-to-end ~1.3x if applied alone, ~1.15x incremental on top of the 3-step-Newton win (claimed 1.13x — confirmed). Effort revised 4-8 h, not 2-4 h.
vetted.reasoning: Mechanism and factor CONFIRMED by an exact replication experiment, but the filter AS SPECIFIED is broken in production and must be amended. (1) Mechanism real: scan_polish_from_coefs (ftperiodogram/core.py:680-713) polishes every max+dip candidate in a vectorized loop linear in candidate count; probe3's counts (7.3 maxima/row H=8, 41.6k total) reproduce exactly. The (pi/M)^2(2H)^2/2 = 1.9% gain bound arithmetic is right (bracketing gives pi/M, not 2pi/M, distance to the nearest sampled neighbor of the true peak), though 'provable' overstates it — P=Re(Y^2/Mm)/YY is rational, not a trig polynomial; the code's own comments (core.py:380-387) treat Bernstein as a feature-scale heuristic with margins. (2) KILL FINDING: the production Paper-2 path calls scan_polish with positive_amplitude=True (multiband.py:425,458,1054 — K.18), and probe3's viability accounting ignored it. My probe (experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_hunt/vet_bernstein_filter.py; replication validated bit-exact vs the real function on non-deferred rows) shows the naive filter changes returned power on 1,277/4,000 rows (32%) at H=8 and 1,670/4,000 (42%) at H=4, max rel change 3-6x, power DECREASING on 1,100 rows — it drops the K.18 constrained winner (best positive-amplitude candidate, routinely below (1-2g)*rowmax). As written this is a SCIENCE-class change, not SAFE. (3) RESCUE VALIDATED: additionally keeping positive-seed candidates within 2*gain of the best positive-seed candidate gives ZERO changed rows (bit-identical powers, 8,000 rows tested, both H) while retaining the win: 41.6k->18.2k candidates (2.28x), polish loop 108.9->42.4 ms (2.57x). Residual non-provable edge (th1 sign can flip between seed and polished point) means risk class is SAFE-with-equivalence-test, never FREE; the equivalence test must run positive_amplitude=True and include sign-flip-adversarial rows. (4) Amdahl checks out: total 274.5 ms at H=8/4000 freqs (matches claimed 269), filter-affected portion ~109 ms; filter alone ~1.32x end-to-end, ~1.15-1.20x incremental after 3-step Newton (claim 1.13x honest). Note the claimed survivor count (1.08 maxima/row) is the broken naive accounting; the correct K.18-safe count is ~1.4 maxima/row — immaterial to the factor. Also the threshold must be rowmax - 2*gain*max|P| (not (1-2g)*rowmax) to be sign-safe, though grid P was nonnegative in all tests.

vetted.name: Direct-sums trig via one complex exp + harmonic recurrence
vetted.mechanism: _direct_stacked_sums_chunk evaluates cos/sin of the full (m, 2H, N) tensor (1.9M trig calls per band-chunk at H=8). Instead compute Z = exp(2i*pi*outer(freqs,t)) once ((m,N), 60k exps) and build harmonics 2..2H by in-place complex multiplication; C+iS and YC+iYS then come from complex matvecs. A further fused variant (accumulate the h-th matvec then Z_cur *= Z, never materializing the (m,2H,N) tensor) should reach ~3x and is exactly the structure the banked GPU direct-sum kernel wants.
vetted.stage: direct summations (53 ms of 269 ms at H=8 direct; 34.5% of wall at H=4)
vetted.factor_stage: 1.8x measured (17.1 -> 9.3 ms per band-chunk), ~3x projected for the fused-matvec variant (25.9 -> ~18 ms projected at H=8 all bands... conservatively sums 53 -> 25 ms)
vetted.factor_end_to_end: 1.12x at H=8; ~1.2x at H=4 (sums are a bigger share); multiplies with the catalog-caching win
vetted.effort: 2-4 h; the naive frequency-cumprod variant is rejected (1.5e-8 drift, only 1.7x)
vetted.evidence: probe5: worst Summations-field diff 2.5e-12 (harmonic recurrence only, <=2H-1 multiplies of error accumulation vs the 1e-7 NFFT tol already accepted on the fast path); timing on (4000,16,15)
vetted.adjusted_factor: Stage: 3.3x measured (fused variant, 14.15→4.21 ms; the materialized recurrence alone gives 2.1x). End-to-end standalone: 1.14x at H=8, 1.34x at H=4 (staged-H detection runs near the H=4 number, so effective ~1.2-1.3x on the detection pass). BUT if the sibling sums-catalog-caching win (probe4) is also banked, the incremental e2e shrinks to ~1.09x (H=4, V=4 templates) / ~1.02x (H=8) — the two wins overlap on the same template-independent stage and do NOT multiply.
vetted.reasoning: Mechanism verified in code: summations.py:320-363 builds the full (m,2H,N) angle tensor and calls np.cos/np.sin on it (1.92M trig evals per band-chunk at (4000,16,15)), and this direct path is the operative one for Paper-2 sparse N (multiband.py:907-921, fast=False). Reproduced the probe single-threaded: trig2 = 2.09x (claimed 1.8x), fused = 3.36x (claimed ~3x projected), worst field diff 2.47e-12 for both (claimed 2.5e-12), i.e. 5 orders below the already-accepted 1e-7 NFFT tolerance — SAFE classification is honest, and deep-dip deferred rows are recomputed via the per-frequency reference path so their bit-match guarantee is unaffected. Stage shares confirmed: sums = 17.3% of H=8 direct wall (claim 19.7%) and 35.8% at H=4 (claim 34.5%); Amdahl arithmetic checks out and the claim is if anything conservative at H=4. Only defect: the 'multiplies with the catalog-caching win' composition claim is wrong — sums are template-independent (multiband.py:896), so catalog caching amortizes exactly this stage; jointly the wins anti-compose (residual ~1.02-1.09x on top of caching). Minor implementation note: fused complex gemv emits spurious Accelerate RuntimeWarnings on macOS (results correct); use real matvecs on .real/.imag views — fits in the 2-4h effort estimate.

vetted.name: Cache template-independent stacked sums across the template catalog (+ slice-share across H stages)
vetted.mechanism: _run_batched calls multiband_power_spectrum_batched once per template-set, and _combine_stacked_shared_amp re-runs _band_stacked_chunk (full trig+einsum on the direct path; fancy-index NFFT extraction on the fast path) per set although the stacked Summations are template-independent. Cache them per (band, chunk) and reuse for all T sets. Bonus: sums for harmonics 1..2H contain sums for any H'<H as a leading slice, so ONE H=8 sums computation can also serve the H=4/H=2 detection stages of the banked staged-H plan. Negative sub-finding: the originally hypothesized template-STACKED scan call (K*nfreq rows in one scan) is NOT worth it -- measured marginal Python/chunk overhead per template is a few ms, not tens.
vetted.stage: catalog-mode sums (56 ms of ~226 ms marginal per extra template, direct path; 12 ms on NFFT path)
vetted.factor_stage: per-extra-template marginal cost 226 -> ~170 ms direct = 1.33x on catalog throughput (1.07x NFFT)
vetted.factor_end_to_end: 1.25-1.33x for a 5-10-template RRL vocabulary run on the direct path; multiplies with all other wins
vetted.effort: 2-4 h (thread a per-band chunk cache through _run_batched / multiband_power_spectrum_batched)
vetted.evidence: probe4: catalog(6)=1466 ms vs 6x single=2002 ms (prep already shared); probe1/2: _band_stacked_chunk = 53-56 ms/template direct, 12 ms NFFT; sums identity across templates is exact (bit-identical reuse)
vetted.adjusted_factor: 1.15-1.25x end-to-end on direct-path catalog detection scans with a 5-10-template vocabulary (measured 1.18x at T=6, bit-identical); ~1.05x on the NFFT path; strictly 1.0x for single-template runs. Drop the H-slice bonus (no factor; net loss under the banked staged-H plan).
vetted.reasoning: Mechanism verified in code: _band_stacked_chunk (multiband.py:912) is template-independent yet recomputed per template-set inside _combine_stacked_shared_amp (line 957) for every catalog member in _run_batched (lines 1307-1310); the non-batched catalog path already shares sums (lines 1262-1275), so this is a parity fix, not a myth, and is not double-counted with banked wins. FREE class verified two ways: batched_YM_MM_from_sums (core.py:93) never mutates its sums input, and a monkeypatched cache probe (probe7_verify_sums_cache.py, single-threaded, T=6, H=8, 4 bands, 15 pts/band, 4000 freqs) produced np.array_equal powers on both direct and NFFT paths with the expected 4-miss/20-hit cache pattern. Factor: measured 1.18x (direct, 1355->1146 ms) and 1.045x (NFFT) at T=6 vs claimed 1.33x/1.07x - claim is the large-T marginal asymptote and slightly optimistic (measured savings ~42 ms/template vs claimed 56), but well within the 2x SOLID band; T=10 extrapolates to ~1.22-1.25x direct. Caveats: applies only to catalog-mode scans (Paper 2 detection stage, which is direct-path at sparse N, so the better number applies); memory for full-grid caching is ~25 MB at 4k freqs/H=8/4 bands (or invert loop order chunk-outer/template-inner to bound it). The claimed H-slice bonus is technically real on the direct path (harmonics 1..2H, sub-block identity holds, though the implementation must retain full 2H-length C/S) but economically backwards given the banked candidate-localized staged-H plan: full-grid H=8 sums cost ~2x H=4 sums, so it only pays if a full-grid H=8 pass runs anyway - contributes no factor and should be removed from the win's accounting.

vetted.name: Powers-only scan path micro-trims (skip params materialization; reuse internal Mv for deferral check)
vetted.mechanism: multiband_power_spectrum_batched discards the params_list that scan_polish_from_coefs builds (per-frequency ModelFitParams namedtuple loop + mbar Horner), and then re-evaluates _eval_polys_on_circle(MM, n_ang) for the deferral check although the scan just computed the identical Mv internally. Add a powers_only flag and return the circle-conditioning (or Mv) from the scan.
vetted.stage: scan tail + deferral check (~6-8 ms of 269 ms at H=8)
vetted.factor_stage: removes ~6-8 ms (duplicate MM FFT ~3 ms measured via circle_fft call #3; params loop ~3-4 ms of scan tottime)
vetted.evidence: probe1: circle_fft n=3 calls (2 needed) totaling 9.1 ms; cProfile scan tottime 27 ms includes the 4000-iteration namedtuple loop; deferral fired on 0/4000 griz rows yet the check FFT is always paid
vetted.adjusted_factor: ~1.02x end-to-end at H=8 (1.013x if NFFT prep counted; 1.018x on the direct-sum path), ~1.04x on the H=4 direct-sum detection stage; survey-mix under staged-H roughly 1.02-1.03x
vetted.reasoning: Both mechanism halves are real in this codebase, verified by reading and by a single-threaded probe (experiments/paper2_gpu/trackB/_hunt/vet_powers_only_trim.py). (1) multiband.py:1059 recomputes _eval_polys_on_circle(MM, n_ang) with the identical MM array and identical angle count (n_ang formula at multiband.py:1049 equals the floor at core.py:573 with default n_angles) that scan_polish_from_coefs already computed as Mv at core.py:582 — measured 4.1 ms at H=8, 1.9 ms at H=4 per 4000-freq chunk. Since _BATCHED_DEFER_RTOL (3e-3) != _SCAN_EXACT_RTOL (0.15) the caller needs absM itself, but returning it from the scan is bit-identical. (2) The params tail (core.py:740-763: complex log, mbar Horner, 4000x ModelFitParams namedtuple loop) is discarded by the batched caller (multiband.py:1054 `_pl, pw, _bp`); powers is assembled before that tail, so skipping is provably output-identical. Measured tail = 1.4 ms — the claimed 3-4 ms was cProfile-inflated, but the dup-FFT is larger than claimed, so total savings = 5.6 ms at H=8 (claim: 6-8 ms) and 3.3 ms at H=4, against 248-313 ms (H=8) / 63-80 ms (H=4) batched stage. FREE class is honest (same FFT on same input; powers untouched; th1/K.18 filter and _exact_root_fallback correctly retained). Factor arithmetic confirmed within ~1.5x of claim: claimed ~1.03x, measured 1.013-1.043x depending on H and whether NFFT prep counts. Effort 1-2 h plausible (powers_only plumbing already exists at the _run level). A real but small win; worth folding in when touching the scan API, not as a standalone session.

vetted.mechanism: Run the full-grid detection scan with n_newton=0 (grid local-max values plus dip-seed evaluations, no Newton polish anywhere), then polish only the top few frequency candidates per source before ranking/refinement. Peak-height underestimate is small and uniform across frequencies and power levels, so the detection statistic (peak vs background, both equally deflated) is plausibly unchanged.
vetted.stage: entire polish machinery within detection (scan 190 -> 81 ms standalone at H=8)
vetted.factor_stage: 2.36x on scan standalone; after wins 1-3 the incremental gain is ~1.15-1.25x end-to-end
vetted.factor_end_to_end: ~1.2x incremental on the already-optimized stack; ~1.7x vs current code if taken alone (269 -> ~160 ms)
vetted.effort: 0.5 day code + a Track-B detection-neutrality measurement (recovery curves polished vs unpolished)
vetted.evidence: probe3: relative deficit median 3.4e-4, p99 2.7e-3, max 4.4e-3 (H=8; H=4: 6.0e-4/4.4e-3/6.6e-3); on top-1%-power rows median 2.2e-4, max 1.3e-3 (no anti-correlation with signal strength); argmax preserved on tested seeds

(2) argmax-preservation evidence is single-seed per H — thin, but the mandated Track-B measurement covers it. No double-counting with banked wins (GPU fused-polish kernel is GPU-lens; this is the CPU path).

vetted.name: Deliberate detection-grid density (os per harmonic-peak, not per 1/T peak)
vetted.mechanism: Peak-height deficit scales as (df*H*T)^2. Choose the detection grid as df = 1/(os*H*T) with os ~= 2.5 and refine candidate frequencies locally (refinement machinery = the banked staged-H refine). Everything downstream of grid size (sums, assembly, scan, polish, GPU kernels) scales linearly with nfreq. WARNING both ways: the current samples_per_peak=5 convention (df=1/(5T)) is only 0.62 pts per 1/(HT) peak at H=8 -- measured worst-case 25% (mean 7%) peak-height loss -- so the H=8 grids in use may be UNDER-sampled for detection while being 2x denser than needed at H=2-4; this lever must be set per detection-H.
vetted.stage: entire per-frequency pipeline (linear in nfreq)
vetted.factor_stage: nfreq ratio: e.g. os=5 -> os=2.5 per harmonic-peak = 2.0x; vs a naive df=1/(40T) H=8 grid, 2x
vetted.factor_end_to_end: ~2x on everything (CPU and GPU), multiplicative with all other wins
vetted.effort: 0.5 day sweep harness + Track-B recovery measurement at 2-3 os values
vetted.evidence: probe6 (10 seeds, random in-cell offset, direct path): worst deficit 3.7%/1.6% at 2.5 pts per 1/(HT) peak (H=4/H=8), 0.12%/0.28% at 5 pts, 25% at 0.62 pts (H=8, today's spp=5); truth = df=1/(200T) local grid

vetted.name: Fused Newton-kernel structural fix: shared-memory coef staging + on-the-fly derivative weights (do this BEFORE writing the kernel)
vetted.mechanism: Register audit of the planned per-thread fused polish: YM(17)+MM(33) = 50 complex128 = 200 32-bit registers for coefficients ALONE, +~40 working registers > the 255/thread ceiling -> guaranteed spills; spilled Horner re-reads ~800 B/thread/Newton-step from local memory, recreating exactly the CuPy precomputed-powers memory-bound failure the FINDINGS already hit. Fix: one block per frequency-tile with coefs in SHARED memory (800 B/freq at H=8, 416 B at H=4; a 16-freq tile = 12.8 KB smem); all candidate-threads of a freq read the same coef word -> hardware broadcast, conflict-free. Do NOT store dY1/dY2/dM1/dM2: fold k and k^2 into the Horner loop (b_j = j*c_j computed on the fly, 1-2 extra FMAs/step) -> only the 2 base coef arrays live in smem (3x less smem+reads). Per-thread registers drop to ~50-70 -> 25-50% occupancy, ample for an FP64-FMA-latency-bound kernel (~4 active warps/SM suffice on GA100).
